name: Reservation Genie
metaDescription: Reservation Genie: a Rails 3 to Rails 8 rewrite of a reservation and ticketing platform for restaurants, tours, and charters, built and led by Alexander Key.
intro: Reservation Genie is a reservation management and ticket sales platform for restaurants, tour operators, and charter companies. It started as a Rails 3 app; I led a small team through a ground-up rewrite to Rails 8 and built its production infrastructure from scratch.
summary: Reservation Genie is a reservation management and ticket sales platform for restaurants and tour operators, processing over seven figures in revenue. It started life as a Rails 3 application; I led a small team through a ground-up rewrite to Rails 8 and built its production infrastructure from scratch.

highlights.title: Rails 3 to Rails 8 rewrite
body: Architected the new application and led a small team through the rewrite, replacing the legacy codebase without interrupting live bookings. Provisioned the servers with Dokku and set up a GitHub Actions pipeline for CI/CD.

highlights.title: Private charter product
body: Designed and built an end-to-end product for tour and boat charter operators: an embeddable lead-capture widget, a prioritized booking pipeline, quote, deposit, and balance invoicing with Stripe, digital waivers, and crew assignment with automated itineraries.

highlights.title: White-labeled booking on client domains
body: Built multi-tenant routing and automated per-client DNS and SSL provisioning so reservations live on client-owned subdomains. Clients can now track Google and Meta ad conversions across the entire booking funnel.

screenshots.alt: Reservation Genie admin dashboard on an iPad showing the day's tour time slots and a table of reservations with statuses and actions

name: Tally Meals
metaDescription: Tally Meals: a ground-up Ruby on Rails rebuild of a Greek house meal management platform with Hotwire Native iOS and Android apps, built and led by Alexander Key.
intro: Tally Meals is a meal reservation platform for college sororities and fraternities. It replaced a failing legacy .NET platform with a ground-up Rails rebuild, and ships iOS and Android apps from the same codebase using Hotwire Native.
summary: Tally Meals is a meal reservation platform for college sororities and fraternities that streamlines communal dining. It replaced a failing legacy .NET platform with a ground-up Rails rebuild, and ships iOS and Android apps from the same codebase using Hotwire Native.

highlights.title: iOS and Android from a single Rails codebase
body: Shipped native mobile apps with Hotwire Native, so members can reserve meals and late plates against chef-published menus on their phones without a separate mobile codebase to maintain.

highlights.title: Chef-published menus and kitchen prep lists
body: Menus can be scheduled daily, weekly, monthly, or for a whole semester. Every meal produces a printable prep list with exact headcounts, late plates, and dietary notes for the kitchen.

highlights.title: Legacy MSSQL to PostgreSQL migration
body: Carried every client's historical data through the replatform by reverse-engineering the old schema and migrating chapters, members, meal plans, and reservation history into the new Rails domain model.

screenshots.alt: Tally Meals mobile app weekly view shown on two phones in light and dark mode

name: 88 Restaurants
metaDescription: 88 Restaurants: a Rails restaurant management platform serving 100+ restaurants with live table management, online ordering, and reservations, built and led by Alexander Key.
intro: 88 Restaurants is an all-in-one restaurant management platform used by 100+ restaurants: live table management, online ordering, and reservations. I led a small team from architecture through launch and owned the full stack for five years.
summary: 88 Restaurants is an all-in-one restaurant management platform used by 100+ restaurants and processing eight figures in payment volume. I led a small team from architecture through launch, owning the full stack from application code and PostgreSQL schema design to production servers and deployment.

highlights.title: Live table management
body: Restaurants draw their real floor plan in a Fabric.js editor and seat guests against it. Table state is synchronized in real time across every device in the restaurant over ActionCable WebSockets, giving front-of-house staff a single live view of the floor.

highlights.title: Online ordering end to end
body: Architected the online ordering system from checkout to fulfillment: Stripe checkout and refunds, an Uber Direct delivery integration, order scheduling, and a full catering system. The system has processed eight figures in payment volume.

highlights.title: Reservations and table sheets
body: A day-by-day reservation list with statuses, paid reservations for prix fixe events, and a table sheet inventory view that lays reservations out against each table's timeline.

screenshots.alt: 88 Restaurants live table management floor plan with the day's reservations and waitlist

name: Austin City Guide
metaDescription: Austin City Guide: a decade-old .NET city guide rebuilt in Ruby on Rails by Alexander Key, now ranking #1 for competitive Austin keywords with 100,000+ monthly visitors.
intro: Austin City Guide is a city guide CMS that I rebuilt from a decade-old .NET codebase in Ruby on Rails as sole developer. It ranks #1 on Google for competitive local keywords and attracts 100,000+ unique visitors a month.
summary: Austin City Guide is a content management system that achieved #1 Google rankings for multiple high-competition keywords such as "things to do in Austin" and now attracts 100,000+ unique visitors monthly. I rebuilt it from a decade-old .NET codebase in Ruby on Rails as sole developer.

highlights.title: #1 Google rankings
body: Ranked first for multiple competitive local keywords, including "things to do in Austin", by combining the Rails rebuild with on-page SEO, technical optimization, and page-speed work. The site now attracts 100,000+ unique visitors a month.

highlights.title: Pay-per-click revenue
body: Featured businesses pay negotiated fees each time a visitor clicks through to their booking page, with every click-through tracked and reported.

highlights.title: In-house analytics and A/B testing
body: Ahoy-based analytics track page traffic, referral sources, time on page, and click-throughs. An A/B split-testing framework built in Rails measured real user behavior and iterated page layouts against live traffic to lift click-through rates on the highest-traffic pages.

screenshots.alt: Austin City Guide homepage on a mobile phone
